questions.question: Which conclave was organized by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) in February 2026 to nurture next-generation research leaders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SANVAD 2026.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) organized SANVAD 2026 from 19th to 21st February 2026 at ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research (NIMR), New Delhi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **SANVAD stands for Scholars’ Assembly for Next-gen Ventures to Advance their Development and is an annual ICMR initiative.**
 
• The three-day conclave brought together around 400 doctoral scholars along with senior scientists, policymakers, and academicians.
 
• The initiative aims to enhance doctoral research quality, innovation orientation, leadership readiness, and institutional collaboration.
 
• The 2027 edition of SANVAD will be hosted by ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)**__

 __
 
• ICMR is India’s apex body for biomedical research.
 
• It functions under the Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• It coordinates and promotes medical research across national institutes and centers.
 
 
 
• **Department of Health Research (DHR)**__
 __
 
• DHR works under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• It supports research in health sciences and policy-linked research initiatives.
 
 
 
• **ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research (NIMR)**__
 
 
• Located in New Delhi.
 
• Specializes in research on malaria and vector-borne diseases.
 
• Hosted the first edition of SANVAD in 2026.

questions.question: Where was the first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly held in India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly** was held in **New Delhi**, India, in **June 2025**.
 
• The IBCA was established to protect and conserve **big cats** such as lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs, jaguars, and snow leopards, which are facing threats due to habitat loss, poaching, and human-wildlife conflict.
 
• The assembly focused on building global cooperation to ensure the long-term conservation and survival of these majestic species.
 
• **New Delhi**, being the capital city of India, was chosen as the venue to emphasize India's commitment to wildlife conservation and its leadership role in the global conservation community.
 
• The event saw participation from member countries, conservation organizations, researchers, and policymakers aiming to strengthen partnerships and share best practices for big cat conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA):**

 
 
• The IBCA was launched as a global initiative by India to protect big cats, with a focus on **cooperative conservation efforts**.
 
• It aims to bring together countries and organizations working on big cat conservation under a unified platform to share knowledge, resources, and strategies.
 
• India has a rich legacy of big cat conservation, including iconic species like the Bengal tiger, Asiatic lion, and leopard.
 
 
 
• **Big Cats and Their Global Importance:**
 
 
• Big cats are apex predators and play a crucial role in maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
 
• Species like tigers, lions, and cheetahs are considered keystone species, meaning their presence ensures the health and stability of their habitats.
 
• Conservation of big cats also has a cultural and economic significance, as they attract ecotourism and are symbols of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in Big Cat Conservation:**
 
 
• India is home to several big cat species, including the **Bengal tiger**, **Asiatic lion**, and **leopard**.
 
• India has successfully implemented conservation programs such as **Project Tiger** (launched in 1973) and **Project Lion** to protect and increase the population of these species.
 
• India also reintroduced cheetahs in 2022 under the **Cheetah Reintroduction Project**, making it a global leader in wildlife conservation.
 
 
 
• **Global Threats to Big Cats:**
 
 
• Big cats face threats such as habitat loss due to deforestation, human encroachment, and urbanization.
 
• Illegal wildlife trade and poaching remain significant challenges, fueled by demand for big cat skins, bones, and other parts.
 
• Human-wildlife conflict is another major issue, particularly in areas where big cats and humans share close proximity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Conservation Efforts:**

 
 
• Organizations like the **World Wildlife Fund (WWF)** and the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** are actively involved in big cat conservation.
 
• Programs such as the **Global Tiger Initiative** and **Snow Leopard Trust** aim to conserve specific big cat species and their habitats.
 
 
 
• **India’s Conservation Milestones:**
 
 
• India hosts over **70% of the world’s tiger population** and has successfully increased their numbers through dedicated conservation efforts.
 
• The **Gir Forest National Park** in Gujarat is the last refuge of the Asiatic lion, and conservation efforts have helped stabilize their population.

questions.question: The 32ⁿd Elets World Education Summit was hosted by which country in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Arab Emirates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **32nd Elets World Education Summit** was hosted in the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** in **April 2025**. This summit is one of the most prestigious events in the education sector, bringing together global leaders, policymakers, educators, and innovators.
 
• The event focused on **transforming education** through technology, innovation, and sustainability, with a special emphasis on addressing the challenges of the post-pandemic world.
 
• The UAE, known for its **progressive approach to education and innovation**, served as an ideal host country for this summit. The country has consistently invested in modernizing its education system and fostering global educational collaborations.
 
• The summit provided a platform for discussions on **emerging trends in education**, such as artificial intelligence in classrooms, the role of EdTech startups, and policies for inclusive education.
 
• It also included **interactive sessions, panel discussions, and exhibitions** showcasing the latest educational tools and technologies, making it a comprehensive event for stakeholders in the education sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Elets World Education Summit:**

 
 
• The Elets World Education Summit is a global platform that fosters collaboration and dialogue between educators, policymakers, and technology providers.
 
• It has been held annually since its inception, covering a wide range of topics such as **digital education, skill development, and global best practices in teaching and learning.**
 
• The summit emphasizes **innovation in education** and how technology can bridge gaps in access and quality of education worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Education in the UAE:**
 
 
• The UAE has made significant strides in education by adopting a vision aligned with its **National Agenda 2021**, focusing on quality education, innovation, and competitiveness.
 
• The country is home to some of the most advanced educational institutions and has hosted numerous global events promoting educational excellence.
 
• The UAE government has prioritized **STEM education, digital literacy, and innovation** in its curriculum to prepare students for the future workforce.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the 32nd Elets Summit:**
 
 
• The summit included participation from over **50 countries**, with delegates discussing global challenges and opportunities in education.
 
• It showcased **cutting-edge technologies** like AI, virtual reality, and blockchain that are reshaping the education landscape.
 
• Special focus was given to **sustainable education practices**, ensuring equitable access to education for all.
 
 
 
• **Other Host Countries in the Past:**
 
 
• Previous editions of the summit have been hosted in countries like **India, South Africa, and the United Kingdom**, highlighting its global outreach.
 
• These events have consistently served as a platform for sharing best practices and fostering partnerships across borders.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why UAE is a Preferred Host:**

 
 
• The UAE is known for its **state-of-the-art infrastructure**, making it a hub for international conferences and summits.
 
• The country has a **diverse population and a strong focus on global collaboration**, which aligns well with the objectives of the Elets World Education Summit.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of the Summit:**
 
 
• Integration of **technology in education** to enhance learning outcomes.
 
• Policy frameworks for achieving **inclusive and equitable education** for all.
 
• Emphasis on **lifelong learning** and skill development to meet the demands of a rapidly changing job market.

questions.question: The inaugural Bharat Steel 2026 Summit is scheduled to be held in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New** Delhi.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Event:** India is set to host the inaugural **Bharat Steel 2026 Summit** on **April 16–17, 2026**.
 
• **Venue:** The summit will be held at **Bharat Mandapam**, Pragati Maidan in **New Delhi**.
 
• **Organizer:** The event is being organized by the **Ministry of Steel**, Government of India, to showcase India’s growing prowess in the global steel landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Focus Themes__**

__
 
• **Green Steel:** A major focus will be on **low-emission and sustainable steel production**, highlighting decarbonization pathways and hydrogen-based steelmaking.
 
• **Industry 4.0:** The summit will explore the role of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and digitalization in optimizing steel plant operations and supply chains.
 
• **Global Hub:** The objective is to position India as a central hub for the global steel industry, attracting foreign investment and technological collaborations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Significance for India__**

 
• **Production Capacity:** India is currently the **second-largest producer of crude steel** in the world, and this summit aims to bolster the "Make in India" initiative.
 
• **Policy Interface:** It provides a platform for high-level dialogue between the government and industry leaders to discuss regulatory frameworks and incentives.
 
• **Resilience:** Discussions will also center on building **resilient global supply chains** for raw materials like coking coal and iron ore.

questions.question: Which country is serving as the chair of the 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) of the World Trade Organization (WTO) held in March 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cameroon.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) of the WTO is being held from March 26–29, 2026, in Yaoundé, Cameroon.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chairmanship:** The conference is chaired by Cameroon’s Minister of Trade, **Mr. Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana**.
 
• **Indian Delegation:** Shri **Piyush Goyal**, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, is leading the Indian delegation at the summit.
 
• **Highest Body:** The Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body of the WTO and usually meets every two years.
 
• **India's Priorities:** India is advocating for a permanent solution for **Public Stockholding (PSH)** for food security and protecting the interests of small-scale fishers.
 
• **WTO Reform:** A major agenda item is restoring a fully functional and binding **Dispute Settlement Mechanism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• World Trade Organization (WTO)__

 __
 
• Established - January 1, 1995 (Successor to GATT)
 
• Headquarters - Geneva, Switzerland
 
• Director-General - Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
 
 
 
• Public Stockholding (PSH)__
 __
 
• This refers to the policy of governments purchasing crops (like rice and wheat) at a **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** to build buffer stocks for food security. India seeks a permanent solution to ensure these subsidies aren't challenged as trade-distorting.
 
 
 
• E-Commerce Moratorium__
 
 
• Since 1998, WTO members have agreed not to impose customs duties on electronic transmissions (like software or e-books). MC14 is debating whether to extend this further.

questions.question: What is the theme of India's BRICS chairship that guided the First Preparatory Meeting of the BRICS Women’s Working Group in 2026?

options.text: Advancing Global Economic Growth and Shared Prosperity
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability
Fostering Women-led Development and Social Transformation
Strengthening Multilateralism for Global Peace and Security

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development** convened the **First Preparatory Meeting of the BRICS Women’s Working Group** under **India’s BRICS Presidency** on **30th April 2026**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The discussions in the meeting were guided by the theme of **India’s BRICS chairship**: **‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability’**.
 
• The meeting focused on **four priority areas** for women globally:
 
 
• **Women in governance and leadership**
 
• **Financial and digital inclusion**
 
• **Women’s entrepreneurship and skill development**

questions.question: In July 2025, the 17th BRICS Summit was held in which of the following country?

__
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** was held in **July 2025** in **Brazil**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***

• **Brazil**
 
• **Russia**
 
• **India**
 
• **China**
 
• **South Africa**

• **Global economic cooperation**
 
• **Trade and investment**
 
• **Climate change**

• **South Africa** – Hosted the 15th BRICS Summit in 2023.
 
• **Russia** – Hosted the 16th BRICS Summit in 2024.
 
• **India** – Not the host of the 2025 summit.
 
• **Brazil** – Hosted the 17th BRICS Summit in 2025. **Correct**.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Brazil.***

questions.question: Which country has hosted the 27th Conference of the Parties to UNFCCC (COP 27)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Egypt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 27th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (**COP 27**) was hosted by **Egypt** in **Sharm El-Sheikh** from **6th to 18th November 2022**.
 
• **Sharm El-Sheikh**, a city on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, was chosen as the venue due to its strategic significance and capacity to accommodate global-scale events.
 
• The COP meetings are held annually to assess progress in dealing with climate change and to negotiate legally binding agreements aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The conference witnessed the participation of **197 parties**, including countries and organizations, under the UNFCCC framework.
 
• A key outcome of COP 27 was the establishment of a **"Loss and Damage" fund**, aimed at compensating vulnerable countries for climate-related damages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):**

 
 
• The UNFCCC was adopted in **1992** at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, as an international environmental treaty to combat climate change.
 
• Its objective is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere to prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
 
• The treaty does not set binding limits on emissions but provides a framework for protocols that can impose such limits.
 
 
 
• **Conference of Parties (COP):**
 
 
• The COP is the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC, where representatives from all member countries meet to assess progress and negotiate climate action measures.
 
• The first COP meeting (COP 1) was held in **Berlin** in **1995**.
 
• Significant outcomes of past COPs include the **Kyoto Protocol** (COP 3, 1997) and the **Paris Agreement** (COP 21, 2015).
 
 
 
• **Key Outcomes of COP 27:**
 
 
• The establishment of the **"Loss and Damage" fund** was a landmark decision to address the needs of developing nations affected by climate change.
 
• Discussions were held on the implementation of the **Glasgow Climate Pact** (adopted at COP 26) to limit global warming to **1.5°C**.
 
• Developed nations were urged to fulfill their pledge of providing **$100 billion annually** to developing countries for climate adaptation and mitigation.
 
 
 
• **About Sharm El-Sheikh:**
 
 
• Sharm El-Sheikh is a coastal city in **Egypt**, located along the Red Sea, and is known for its role as a venue for international conferences and summits.
 
• The city is also a hub for eco-tourism and marine biodiversity, making it a fitting location for a climate-focused event like COP 27.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• Adopted in **2015** at COP 21, the Paris Agreement aims to limit global warming to well below **2°C** above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit it to **1.5°C**.
 
• It requires countries to submit their **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, outlining their plans to reduce emissions and adapt to climate impacts.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **1997** at COP 3, the Kyoto Protocol legally binds developed countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• It introduced mechanisms like **Clean Development Mechanism (CDM)** and **carbon trading** to achieve emission reduction targets.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Challenges:**
 
 
• Rising global temperatures, sea-level rise, and extreme weather events are urgent challenges addressed at COP meetings.
 
• The focus remains on enhancing renewable energy adoption, phasing out fossil fuels, and promoting sustainable development.
